title: Fix-cycle get_range length-clamp has no regression test
body: OCFL store.py get_range caps length = min(length, max_range_bytes, max_read_buffer_bytes) and reads via _read_bounded. No test ever engages this cap: the source_store fixture sets max_range_bytes=4096, but no test puts >4096 bytes nor requests length>4096, so the clamp branch is dead in tests. test_put_get_roundtrip_and_fixity only asserts the `truncated` FLAG on a 9-byte range (end<total), and test_get_range_out_of_bounds_is_clamped only clamps an out-of-bounds START. Oversize REJECTION (put side, max_upload_bytes) IS tested (test_oversize_payload_rejected). The fix's distinguishing behavior (read-side bounded clamp to max_read_buffer_bytes) is unasserted. Files: tests/storage/test_ocfl_store.py, src/umd/storage/ocfl/store.py:198/307. Severity: MINOR (memory-safety bound; code correct); caller explicitly listed it as a must-verify fix-cycle item.

title: Ledger.append ON CONFLICT race-fallback branch not exercised
body: SemanticLedger.append has a top-of-function pre-check (ledger.py:89-94) that returns the existing seq for a duplicate idempotency_key BEFORE the INSERT. So test_idempotency_key_dedup_does_not_duplicate_completion (sequential duplicate append) returns early and never reaches the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + select fallback (ledger.py:141-153) — that race branch is uncovered. The CONTRACT (same token, no duplicate rows) IS asserted, and the DB UNIQUE constraint enforces it. Contrast: StageRunRepository.claim has NO pre-check — its sequential duplicate test genuinely exercises the ON CONFLICT + select-fallback path (stage_repository.py:131-149). Severity: MINOR/defensive (true race hard to test deterministically).

title: Evidence record() not idempotent across calls (Check B)

title: FLAKY test_p5_s1_public_identity_e2e — root cause verified (implementation bug)
body: CONFIRMED 2/7 failures in isolation (reported ~20-25%). Symptom: AssertionError at test_api_contract.py:2041 — "'the apprentice' in []" (Mara aliases empty; synthetic canonical label='the apprentice' aliases=['Moss'] appears). ROOT CAUSE (verified via instrumented _UnionFind.union trace + Pass 2b simulation, /tmp/union_out2.txt): provider alias mentions carry canonical_name INSIDE their normalized_forms ('the apprentice' → forms=['mara','the apprentice'], 'Moss' → forms=['mara','moss']). Pass 2b in src/umd/resolution/service.py:399-410 links each alias mention to the FIRST mention_id-sorted target whose forms contain the canonical name; when two alias mentions pair with EACH OTHER (apprentice↔Moss) instead of the real Mara mention — decided by random mention_id ordering (mention ids embed per-ingest uuid4 source_id) — they form a synthetic canonical and Mara loses aliases. The `break` on first match seals the bad pairing; Pass 2b NEVER fires against a real Mara mention in any traced run. ALSO: canonical refs differ across fresh ingests of the same book (Mara = 5cbedbc4 / 73f2652c / 086256a6) — deterministic per-ingest only, because canonical_entity_ref digests member mention_ids that embed the random source_id. This is a test-correct/implementation-wrong case → MAJOR_RAISE.
